column2: ENGLISH
Ask for Ships
Ask [Root.GetTitledName] to lend galleys from their own ports for this war. The ships sail under your command until peace. You pay their crews' wages, and a tenth more to [Root.GetTitledName].
We are at war, and neither borrow nor lend ships now
They have a shipyard, arsenal, harbour or family palace in a holding of their own, and neither borrow nor lend ships now
We choose how many galleys to ask for
[afl_lender.GetTitledName] will consider our request
Our galleys sail to [afl_borrower.GetTitledName] at once
Recall Our Ships
Call home the ships we have lent. They will leave our ally within the month.
Ships Away
A tenth of this holding's galleys serve an ally.
Ships Away
A hundredth of this holding's galleys serve an ally.
How many galleys should we ask [afl_lender.GetTitledName] for? Their own ports can spare up to [Root.afl_base.GetValue]. We would pay the crews' wages, and a tenth more to them.
How large a fleet should we ask [afl_lender.GetTitledName] for? Their own ports can spare up to [Root.afl_base.GetValue]. We would pay the crews' wages, and a tenth more to them.
50 galleys, for 5,000 men: about 16.5 gold a month
100 galleys, for 10,000 men: about 33 gold a month
More galleys: 150 or 200
On second thought, we will manage without.
150 galleys, for 15,000 men: about 49.5 gold a month
200 galleys, for 20,000 men: about 66 gold a month
More galleys: 300 to 500
On second thought, we will manage without.
300 galleys, for 30,000 men: about 99 gold a month
400 galleys, for 40,000 men: about 132 gold a month
500 galleys, for 50,000 men: about 165 gold a month
On second thought, we will manage without.
[afl_lender.GetTitledName] has only [Root.afl_base.GetValue] galleys in their own ports, too few to spare fifty. Their vassals' ships are not theirs to lend.

[afl_borrower.GetTitledName], our partner in this war, asks us to lend [Root.afl_ask.GetValue] galleys until peace. They would pay the crews' wages, and a tenth more to us: [Root.afl_margin.GetValue] gold a month. While the ships are away, each of our own holdings with a shipyard would raise [Root.afl_k.GetValue]% fewer galleys. Our vassals keep theirs.
Lend them the ships.
We need our ships.
The galleys of [afl_lender.GetTitledName] have come, [Root.afl_ask.GetValue] of them, and await our orders at sea. They will sail home when the war ends.
Excellent.
[afl_lender.GetTitledName] has refused to lend us ships.
So be it.
The crews of the galleys [afl_lender.GetTitledName] lent [afl_borrower.GetTitledName] went unpaid this month: the treasury is in debt. If they go unpaid next month too, the ships will sail home.
Noted.
The galleys of [afl_lender.GetTitledName] serving [afl_borrower.GetTitledName] have gone home, and their contract is over.
So ends the loan.

Our predecessor lent [Root.afl_ask.GetValue] galleys to [afl_borrower.GetTitledName] for their war, and those ships still serve them, for their wages and a tenth more to us. We may let the loan run until peace, or recall the ships.
Let them serve.
Hire Ships

Hire galleys with their crews from the ports of [Root.GetTitledName], not their vassals', for a year. They wait off a port of [Root.GetTitledName] from the day the charter is signed, under your command. You pay two months' wages on signing, then the crews' wages and a quarter more to [Root.GetTitledName] each month.
Offer Ships for Hire

Offer [Root.GetTitledName] galleys with their crews from your own ports, for a year. They wait off one of your ports from the day the charter is signed, under the command of [Root.GetTitledName]. [Root.GetTitledName] pays you two months' wages on signing, then the crews' wages, and a quarter more to you each month.
We hold land, and neither borrow nor lend ships now
They hold land, and neither borrow nor lend ships now
We have a shipyard, arsenal, harbour or family palace in a holding of our own, and neither borrow nor lend ships now
We choose how many galleys to offer
[afl_borrower.GetTitledName] will consider our offer
We receive [Root.afl_lump.GetValue] gold now, and our ships wait off [afl_port.GetName] under their command
We pay [Root.afl_lump.GetValue] gold now, and the ships wait off [afl_port.GetName] under our command

Our predecessor hired out [Root.afl_ask.GetValue] galleys to [afl_borrower.GetTitledName] for a year, and those ships still serve them, for the crews' wages and a quarter more to us. The charter runs its term.

How many galleys should we hire from [afl_lender.GetTitledName]? Their own ports can spare up to [Root.afl_base.GetValue]. The ships would wait off one of their ports from the day of signing, and serve us a year. We would pay two months' wages on signing, then the crews' wages and a quarter more to them each month. Only what we can pay on signing is offered.
[afl_lender.GetTitledName] has only [Root.afl_base.GetValue] galleys in their own ports, too few to spare fifty. Their vassals' ships are not theirs to hire out.
50 galleys, for 5,000 men: 30 gold now, then about 18.75 a month
100 galleys, for 10,000 men: 60 gold now, then about 37.5 a month
150 galleys, for 15,000 men: 90 gold now, then about 56.25 a month
200 galleys, for 20,000 men: 120 gold now, then about 75 a month
300 galleys, for 30,000 men: 180 gold now, then about 112.5 a month
400 galleys, for 40,000 men: 240 gold now, then about 150 a month
500 galleys, for 50,000 men: 300 gold now, then about 187.5 a month
More galleys: 150 or 200
On second thought, we will manage without.
More galleys: 300 to 500
On second thought, we will manage without.
On second thought, we will manage without.

[afl_borrower.GetTitledName] asks to hire [Root.afl_ask.GetValue] of our galleys, with their crews, for a year. They would pay us [Root.afl_lump.GetValue] gold on signing, the crews' wages, and [Root.afl_margin.GetValue] gold a month more. The ships would wait off [afl_port.GetName] from the day of signing. While they are away, each of our own holdings with a shipyard would raise [Root.afl_k.GetValue]% fewer galleys. Our vassals keep theirs.
[afl_borrower.GetTitledName] asks to hire [Root.afl_ask.GetValue] of our galleys, but can no longer pay the [Root.afl_lump.GetValue] gold due on signing.
Sign the charter.
We need our ships.

[afl_lender.GetTitledName] has signed the charter: [Root.afl_ask.GetValue] galleys with their crews, for a year. We have paid [Root.afl_lump.GetValue] gold. The ships wait off [afl_port.GetName], under our command.

[afl_borrower.GetTitledName] has signed our charter for [Root.afl_ask.GetValue] galleys and paid us [Root.afl_lump.GetValue] gold. Our ships wait off [afl_port.GetName], under their command, for a year.
Very well.
The charter of the galleys [afl_lender.GetTitledName] hired out to [afl_borrower.GetTitledName] ends next month, and the ships will sail home. Any army aboard should be put ashore before then.
Noted.

How many galleys should we offer [afl_borrower.GetTitledName]? Our own ports can spare up to [Root.afl_base.GetValue]. They would wait off one of our ports from the day of signing, and serve a year. [afl_borrower.GetTitledName] would pay us two months' wages on signing, then the crews' wages and a quarter more to us each month.
Our own ports hold only [Root.afl_base.GetValue] galleys, too few to spare fifty. Our vassals' ships are not ours to hire out.
50 galleys, for 5,000 men: 30 gold on signing, 3.75 a month to us
100 galleys, for 10,000 men: 60 gold on signing, 7.5 a month to us
150 galleys, for 15,000 men: 90 gold on signing, 11.25 a month to us
200 galleys, for 20,000 men: 120 gold on signing, 15 a month to us
300 galleys, for 30,000 men: 180 gold on signing, 22.5 a month to us
400 galleys, for 40,000 men: 240 gold on signing, 30 a month to us
500 galleys, for 50,000 men: 300 gold on signing, 37.5 a month to us
More galleys: 150 or 200
On second thought, we keep our ships.
More galleys: 300 to 500
On second thought, we keep our ships.
On second thought, we keep our ships.

[afl_lender.GetTitledName] offers to hire us [Root.afl_ask.GetValue] galleys with their crews, for a year. We would pay [Root.afl_lump.GetValue] gold on signing, then the crews' wages of about [Root.afl_wages.GetValue] gold a month and [Root.afl_margin.GetValue] more to them. The ships would wait off [afl_port.GetName] from the day of signing, under our command.
[afl_lender.GetTitledName] offers to hire us [Root.afl_ask.GetValue] galleys, but we can't pay the [Root.afl_lump.GetValue] gold due on signing.
Sign the charter.
We have no need of them.
[afl_borrower.GetTitledName] has declined our offer of ships.
So be it.
